raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Tighten the CUDA fused-path dispatch in `Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer.self_attention` so it is selected only when the positions tensor is one-dimensional, matching the fused kernel's documented `[T]` contract. Let multidimensional mRoPE positions fall through to the existing native preparation branch, which already applies Q/K normalization and `rotary_emb` with all position axes and requires no new abstraction or kernel behavior. Add a focused CPU-CI unit test that stubs the preparation and attention operations to verify both sides of the dispatch boundary without requiring a model checkpoint or CUDA hardware.

Qwen3.5 vision-language requests pass a three-axis mRoPE position tensor into `Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer.self_attention`, but the CUDA fused QK normalization/RoPE/gate kernel consumes positions as a one-dimensional token sequence. This silently applies the wrong rotary coordinates and produces severely displaced image-grounding boxes, while forcing the existing native preparation path restores parity with vLLM. The failure is independently reproduced on two Blackwell GPUs with both NVFP4 and official FP8 weights, so it is not confined to a quantized vision encoder. Text-only inputs with one-dimensional positions should retain the fused fast path.

Fixes #35949

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py`: gate the fused CUDA path on a
  one-dimensional positions tensor; multidimensional mRoPE positions fall
  through to the existing native preparation branch.
- `test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_5_mrope_dispatch.py`: CPU-only unit
  test stubbing preparation and attention to assert both sides of the
  dispatch boundary, with no checkpoint or CUDA required.

## Accuracy Tests

Not run. The dispatch boundary is covered by the unit test above; the
end-to-end image-grounding parity described in #35949 was reported by the
issue author on Blackwell hardware and has not been independently reproduced
here.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. Text-only inputs keep the fused fast path unchanged, so no
throughput change is expected for them; this has not been benchmarked.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

nodes.body:
We encountered the same issue. This is a fairly severe correctness bug affecting multimodal requests.

On the same 200-example chart understanding QA evaluation (internal dataset), our self-hosted Qwen3.8-27B served with SGLang scored 65.5–71% across different runs, compared with 83.2% on Alibaba's official hosted endpoint. With this patch applied, the self-hosted model reached 82.8% average accuracy across different runs, effectively closing the gap.

Thanks for identifying and fixing this!

cc. @chenyang08056032 for visibility

Resurfacing this thread. @mvanhorn @chenyang08056032 @yhyang201 
Can we resolve the failed tests and merge this PR? 🙏 This bug is critical for Qwen-3.5+ deployment.

@Haoxiang-Wang I went through the failing checks one at a time, and none of them are caused by this patch. I have just updated the branch onto current `main`, so the reruns should show most of this clearing on their own.

Per check:

- Base `call-gate / pr-gate` actually passed. Its only test failure was `test_deepseek_v4_shared_expert_fusion.py`, from an uninitialized MoE parallel group. Current `main` already carries the test setup that initializes it, so the branch update should resolve that one.
- Extra call gate failed with `Missing required label 'run-ci-extra'`. No tests ran at all. That one needs a maintainer to add the label; I cannot set it myself.
- NPU: the custom container implementation failed and the job asked for a runner administrator.
- AMD: an unrelated Qwen1.5-MoE server process exited `-9`.
- XPU: `test_xpu_embedding.py` timed out twice.
- Xeon: the Intel AMX test download failed with HTTP 403.
- The remaining `finish` and wait-job failures are downstream aggregation of the above.

On the patch itself, I checked the dispatch behavior directly rather than through the full suite, because this environment lacks `triton`: with mRoPE 3-D positions the native preparation path is taken, and with text 1-D positions the fused CUDA path is taken. Both assertions pass. The test is registered correctly for CI (`suite=base-a-test-cpu`, `est_time=2.0`).

So the remaining ask is just the `run-ci-extra` label if Extra CI is required for this to merge. Happy to rebase again if anything else drifts.

@Haoxiang-Wang this PR no longer needs to merge. #34446 landed on main on Aug 30 and fixed the same bug in the kernel itself: `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate` now takes an `mrope_axis_map` and reads the height and width rows, and `qwen3_5.py` passes that map whenever positions are 2-D.

I missed that in my last comment, so ignore what I said there about the `run-ci-extra` label. With the kernel fixed, the `positions.ndim == 1` check here would only take multimodal requests off a fused path that now handles them. The branch also conflicts with main because that dispatch moved into `_prepare_qkv_gate`, and rebasing it isn't worth doing. This can be closed.

I checked this by reading the code on main, not by rerunning your eval. If you still see the accuracy gap on a build that includes #34446, that's a separate bug and worth a new issue with the build and numbers.

<!-- r:79d580ee104a.9106a0aa3e27 -->

Closing this in favor of #34446 (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34446), which merged on Aug 30 and fixed the bug in the fused kernel itself. See my comment above for the details.

<!-- r:79d580ee104a.ce480bdbe7e3 -->

files.patch:
@@ -1350,7 +1350,7 @@ def self_attention(
         forward_batch: ForwardBatch,
     ) -> torch.Tensor:
         """Full attention forward pass."""
-        if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate:
+        if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate and positions.ndim == 1:
             q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_cuda_fused(
                 positions=positions,
                 hidden_states=hidden_states,

@@ -0,0 +1,89 @@
+"""CPU-only tests for Qwen3.5 attention preparation dispatch."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.models import qwen3_5
+from sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5 import Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestQwen3_5MropeDispatch(CustomTestCase):
+    def _run_self_attention(self, positions):
+        prepared = tuple(object() for _ in range(4))
+        attention_output = torch.ones(2, 4)
+        gated_output = torch.full((2, 4), 2.0)
+        projected_output = torch.full((2, 4), 3.0)
+        layer = SimpleNamespace(
+            attn_output_gate=True,
+            forward_prepare_cuda_fused=mock.Mock(return_value=prepared),
+            forward_prepare_fused_gate=mock.Mock(),
+            forward_prepare_native=mock.Mock(return_value=prepared),
+            forward_prepare_npu=mock.Mock(),
+            attn=mock.Mock(return_value=attention_output),
+            o_proj=mock.Mock(return_value=(projected_output, None)),
+        )
+        hidden_states = torch.zeros(2, 4)
+        forward_batch = object()
+
+        with (
+            mock.patch.multiple(
+                qwen3_5,
+                _is_cuda=True,
+                _is_hip=False,
+                _is_xpu=False,
+                _is_cpu=False,
+                _is_npu=False,
+            ),
+            mock.patch.object(
+                qwen3_5,
+                "fused_sigmoid_mul",
+                return_value=gated_output,
+            ) as sigmoid_mul,
+        ):
+            output = Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer.self_attention(
+                layer,
+                positions=positions,
+                hidden_states=hidden_states,
+                forward_batch=forward_batch,
+            )
+
+        layer.attn.assert_called_once_with(*prepared[:3], forward_batch)
+        sigmoid_mul.assert_called_once_with(attention_output, prepared[3], inplace=True)
+        layer.o_proj.assert_called_once_with(gated_output)
+        layer.forward_prepare_fused_gate.assert_not_called()
+        layer.forward_prepare_npu.assert_not_called()
+        self.assertIs(output, projected_output)
+        return layer
+
+    def test_mrope_positions_use_native_preparation(self):
+        positions = torch.arange(6).reshape(3, 2)
+
+        layer = self._run_self_attention(positions)
+
+        layer.forward_prepare_native.assert_called_once_with(
+            positions=positions,
+            hidden_states=mock.ANY,
+        )
+        layer.forward_prepare_cuda_fused.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_text_positions_use_cuda_fused_preparation(self):
+        positions = torch.arange(2)
+
+        layer = self._run_self_attention(positions)
+
+        layer.forward_prepare_cuda_fused.assert_called_once_with(
+            positions=positions,
+            hidden_states=mock.ANY,
+        )
+        layer.forward_prepare_native.assert_not_called()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
